text:
marie (support): pinging eng-sre + runtime — AcmePayments (dedicated customer) opened an escalation: p99 for text generation jumped ~6x starting ~2026-03-15T03:00Z. They said requests either queue for ~4–6s or fail with 502. Customer says this impacted checkout flows. attaching logs they pasted.

jake (eng-sre): @marie can you paste the pool id and a couple of request ids? we'll need traces and fleetmgr logs.

marie (support): pool dp-09. request ids: r_0a1b2c3d, r_0a1b2c4e. They included a trace link: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/r_0a1b2c3d (internal). Customer timestamped around 03:02-03:08 UTC.

li (eng-runtime): thanks — looking at tracing, I see a long wait in attach path: "wait_for_gpu -> attach_delay -> warmup_kernel". p95 stays OK but p99 shows the long attach_delay. suspect late attach/cold-gpu.

ana (oncall): @li can you paste the fleet manager logs around those times? I'm also seeing pool saturation metrics: active_requests ~200, queued ~80.

li (eng-runtime): grabbing fleetmgr logs now, filtered for dp-09. snippet below:

```
2026-03-15T03:01:02.124Z WARN fleetmgr attach_delay_ms=5123 pool=dp-09 reason="waiting_for_gpu"
2026-03-15T03:01:02.125Z INFO pool dp-09 capacity=40 active=38 pending_attach=12 queued_requests=24
2026-03-15T03:01:05.998Z WARN attach failed id=r_0a1b2c3d err="gpu-warmup-timeout"
2026-03-15T03:02:10.442Z INFO autoscaler scaleup_request pool=dp-09 desired=45 current=40 throttle=true backoff_ms=1200
2026-03-15T03:02:11.003Z INFO provisioning queue depth=6 throttled_by_capacity=true
```

li (eng-runtime): fleetmgr shows autoscaler requested scale-up but provisioning path got throttled; attach backoff climbed.

jake (eng-sre): that logs out pretty clearly: scale-up request made but the cloud provider (or provisioning controller) returned throttle / delayed provisioning. we have two orthogonal issues: 1) dedicated pool hitting capacity (saturation) and 2) cold GPU warmup lengthening attach. both increase p99.

marie (support): customer said this started after yesterday's runtime kernel bump (quant-kernel v2) — could be correlated. they see more warmup failures since the bump.

li (eng-runtime): good catch. I can repro warmup taking longer on v2 kernels in staging when model sequence len > 1024. I'll roll an instrumentation build to capture kernel init time.

sam (customer-success): customer is very sensitive — they asked for temporary mitigation while we investigate. business impact: checkout conversion drop. asking for ETA.

ana (oncall): immediate mitigations we can consider: - increase reserved_burst for AcmePayments in dp-09 (if pool supports per-customer reservation) - enable a tiny warm pool (pre-warmed instances) for dp-09 for next 2h - reduce attach_backoff_ms threshold to accept faster attaches (tradeoff: more attach churn) - route traffic for AcmePayments to fallback hosted model (lower perf but available)

jake (eng-sre): I propose we do, in order: 1) temporarily bump reserved burst for dp-09 customer to 20% of pool (so new requests get allocated capacity) 2) increase warm_pool_size to 2 for dp-09 3) revert quant-kernel v2 rollout for dp-09 model family (staged rollback) — if runtime confirms kernel regression.

li (eng-runtime): I will validate kernel repro. If confirmed, I can push a targeted rollback for dp-09's model variant (no global rollback). For telemetry we should enable a short-term metric: kernel_init_ms and gpu_attach_ms.

marie (support): customer asked for a SLA-style confirmation. can we give them an action plan + ETA?

jake (eng-sre): ETA: 15 min to apply reserved_burst + warm_pool change, 30–45 min to confirm p99 reduction. rollback of kernel: ~45–60 min if we can stage it (depends on artifact availability). I'll coordinate.

li (eng-runtime): running quick checks now. command I'm using to inspect pool: `fleetctl get-pool dp-09 --json` output (sanitized):

```
{"pool_id":"dp-09","capacity":40,"active":39,"pending_attach":14,"reserved_burst_pct":0,"warm_pool_size":0}
```

li (eng-runtime): I'm going to apply reserved_burst=20 and warm_pool_size=2 for dp-09. running: `fleetctl patch-pool dp-09 --set reserved_burst_pct=20 --set warm_pool_size=2`

deploy-bot: deploy accepted: patch-pool dp-09 by li at 2026-03-15T03:12:21Z (change-id ch_9876).

li (eng-runtime): change applied. new pool state: `active=39 pending_attach=10 warm_pool=2` — we already see one warm instance coming online.

ana (oncall): can we also open an incident ticket so we track customer comms and RCA? I'll open INC-1965012345 and link here.

marie (support): opened INC-1965012345 and emailed customer with interim mitigation steps + ETA. they acknowledged and asked for updates every 30 min.

li (eng-runtime): telemetry after changes: p99 for that customer dropped from ~6s to ~900ms in the first 5 minutes for sampled traces. still seeing occasional 2.5s spikes that map to provisioning throttles. autoscaler logs now: `scaleup_request desired=45 throttle=false` — so reserved burst took pressure off.

jake (eng-sre): good. next actions: - run kernel init timing tests in staging to confirm quant-kernel v2 regression (li) - identify why provisioning was throttled (cloud quotas / internal rate limiter) — I'll check provisioning controller and cloud quotas - create a follow-up to make warm_pool_size configurable per-customer on dedicated pools (product).

li (eng-runtime): quick repro in staging: kernel_init_ms median on v1=120ms, v2=520ms for long sequences. I'll capture a micro-benchmark and open PR to revert v2 for dp-09 model variant.

jake (eng-sre): provisioning throttles: saw message from provisioner: `throttle_reason=attach_rate_limit` with recent backoff config set to 1200ms. seems we need a smarter backoff policy (exponential + jitter) and a burst allowance for Dedicated. filing infra task.

sam (customer-success): customer appreciated the quick mitigation, asked to be notified when we revert the kernel. I'll own the comms.

li (eng-runtime): started targeted rollback for dp-09 models to quant-kernel v1. command: `deployctl promote artifact:quant-kernel:v1 --target pool=dp-09 --strategy=rolling --batch=2` — kicked off at 03:28.

deploy-bot: rollout started: quant-kernel:v1 -> dp-09 (batch size 2). track: https://rollouts.redwood.internal/roll/rl_2048

li (eng-runtime): monitoring warmup times as batches finish. initial batches show kernel_init_ms back to ~130ms. p99 trending toward baseline.

jake (eng-sre): I'll follow up on quota/throttle: raising priority to P1 for infra. we should also add a short-term rule to prefer local capacity (avoid cross-region spawns) when pool saturation is near threshold.

marie (support): customer updated: conversion recovering, very grateful. they requested postmortem and whether we can guarantee no recurrence.

ana (oncall): agreed — we'll produce RCA: root cause = combination of kernel v2 increasing warmup time + provisioning throttles + no per-customer warm_pool config. mitigations: immediate reserved burst & warm_pool change + targeted rollback; long-term: fix kernel, add prewarm config, improve backoff/provisioning policy, add kernel_init_ms metric and alert.

marie (support): putting this thread into incident INC-1965012345 and will create a follow-up for the RCA doc. closing loop with customer now. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:

jake (eng-sre): thanks team. I'll own the infra follow-ups.

li (eng-runtime): I'll post the kernel benchmarks and PR links in the incident doc.

sam (customer-success): will send customer summary once rollback completes.

marie (support): thread archived into INC-1965012345 — end of thread.
